purpose: External eval set for vibe-requirements-spec. Prompts live outside skills/ so they are not bundled as skill content. Covers Markdown requirements-spec artifact drafting before implementation planning, same-spec revision, explicit approval persistence, small-request question limits, broad confirmation checklists, creative requirement exploration, downstream-workflow neutrality, non-technical communication, scope boundaries, defaults versus decisions, write-safety, auditability, contradiction handling, and stop behavior after approval or handoff wording.
common_assertions: Output creates or updates a Markdown requirements spec artifact at an explicit path and returns a concise chat summary with spec path, approval state, blockers or unknowns, and exact next user action.

While the skill is active, output does not create implementation plans, implementation task entries, code changes, tests, verification command lists, commits, release work, changelog edits, or unrelated files.

Output separates confirmed requirements, proposed defaults, ideas or options, user decisions, assumptions, out-of-scope items, acceptance criteria, open risks or unknowns, and approval state instead of blending them into a single recommendation.
Output uses an approval state such as Draft, Awaiting explicit approval, Approved, or Reopened after approval; it does not use planning-readiness labels as the handoff contract.
Readiness, confirmation, completed checklist, handoff, or `go ahead` wording is not treated as approval unless it clearly approves the current spec artifact.
If the conversation or artifact already identifies a spec path, output updates that same spec instead of creating a new unrelated spec.
Output does not require, name, or route to a specific downstream skill or workflow; it may refer generically to a later implementation-planning phase after approval.
If output includes `Can default`, defaults do not select or pre-stage behavior for unselected adjacent surfaces with conditional wording such as `within whichever ... you select`.
For broad or highly unclear requests with more than three material decisions, output uses a grouped confirmation checklist in the spec rather than a long interrogation.
When creative exploration is useful, output presents brainstormed ideas as candidate options with tradeoffs and does not treat unchosen ideas as confirmed requirements.
Output marks inferred behavior as an assumption or proposed default, not as a confirmed user requirement.
Output keeps adjacent features out of scope unless the user explicitly includes them in the first useful slice.

Output does not put unconfirmed adjacent capabilities in confirmed requirements with a `subject to confirmation` qualifier; they stay in out-of-scope items, decisions needed, or candidate options until selected.
Output uses the user's language for the chat-facing summary while preserving code identifiers, paths, commands, API names, and product terms.

evals.name: Small profile UI spec
evals.prompt: I want users to be able to edit their display name on the profile screen, but I have not decided the details yet. Make it feel right.
evals.expected_output: The agent creates a Markdown requirements spec for display-name editing, proposes a small first scope, asks at most three direct questions in the summary, sets approval state to Awaiting explicit approval or Draft, and stops without writing an implementation plan.
expectations: Creates or updates a requirements spec artifact at an explicit path.
Uses the user's active language for the user-facing summary.
Keeps the first scope limited to display-name editing.
Separates confirmed goal from assumptions or proposed defaults such as save behavior, validation, and cancel/reset behavior.
Asks no more than three direct questions.
Provides concrete reasonable defaults that the user can accept with one short approval instead of pairing every unresolved detail with an open question.
If multiple interaction, validation, or save-behavior options are presented, marks one as the recommended default rather than requiring the user to choose every value.
Defines practical acceptance criteria such as editing, saving, validation, and visible feedback without claiming implementation details.
Does not plan code edits, tests, files other than the spec, or commits.

evals.name: Broad notification request uses checklist
evals.prompt: I want the whole notification area to feel right. Email, SMS, push notifications, frequency settings, an admin screen, and delivery logs all sound useful. What do we need to decide?
evals.expected_output: The agent creates or updates a requirements spec with a grouped confirmation checklist that separates blocking first-scope decisions, safe defaults for chosen scope, and later decisions; admin screens and delivery logs stay out of the first slice until explicitly selected.
expectations: Uses a confirmation checklist in the spec instead of asking many direct questions.
Groups items into blocking decisions, defaults that can be accepted or overridden, and later decisions.
Recommends a bounded first useful scope that does not include admin screens or delivery logs unless the user explicitly selects them.
Explains SMS and push uncertainty in product terms such as cost, permission, provider setup, or opt-in behavior without inventing provider facts.
Keeps admin screens and delivery logs out of confirmed requirements and first-slice defaults unless the user explicitly selects them.

Does not place admin capabilities, delivery-log storage, delivery-log retention, or delivery-log search in `Can default`, even with `if selected later`, `within whichever ... you select`, or `confirm once chosen` wording.
Sets approval state based on unresolved channel and behavior decisions.
Does not name or require a specific downstream workflow.

evals.name: Immediate coding request still drafts spec
evals.prompt: Just start coding a CSV import feature. I only know it should upload a file and somehow create contacts.
evals.expected_output: The agent creates or updates a requirements spec instead of coding because file format, validation, duplicate handling, preview behavior, permissions, persistence, and recovery rules are underspecified.
expectations: Does not provide code, patches, non-spec file edits, or implementation steps.
Identifies upload surface and CSV parsing or file-format choices as build-changing decisions or unknowns.
Identifies validation or row-error behavior and duplicate or conflict handling as build-changing decisions or defaults.
Explicitly identifies review-before-write or preview behavior as a build-changing decision, default, out-of-scope item, or open unknown; a post-import result summary alone is not enough.
Identifies permissions, persistence, and rollback or recovery as build-changing decisions, defaults, out-of-scope items, or open unknowns.
Separates a minimal proposed first scope from later enhancements.
Uses a checklist or concise decision list if more than three material choices are open.
Keeps approval state unapproved until blocking data and behavior decisions or local evidence checks are answered.
If both user decisions and local evidence checks still affect planning reliability or the build shape, the summary names both instead of treating the user reply as the only gate.
Does not call local evidence checks routine when they can change scope, data contracts, success criteria, safety, compatibility, or recovery expectations.
Does not call existing schema, validation, create-path, upload-plumbing, or file-limit checks routine if they can change import columns, mapping, limits, persistence, success criteria, or safety.
Explicitly treats `somehow create contacts` as an unresolved data contract, not a confirmed mapping, persistence, or duplicate-handling rule.

evals.name: Downstream workflow neutrality
evals.prompt: Before any planning tool or special workflow gets involved, help me clarify a billing settings change. Users should be able to choose invoice email recipients, but I don't want this tied to a specific agent skill.
evals.expected_output: The agent drafts a billing-recipient requirements spec and avoids naming, requiring, or routing to any downstream skill or workflow.
expectations: Does not name or require any downstream skill, planning tool, or special workflow.
Clarifies billing-recipient behavior, permissions, and validation at the requirement level.
Clarifies auditability as a requirement dimension, such as whether recipient changes are logged, attributable, retained, or visible, rather than only putting audit-log UI out of scope.
Clarifies notification consequences at the requirement level, such as which future invoice emails are affected after saving recipient changes.
Marks billing and permission choices as blocking or high-impact decisions where appropriate.
Keeps adjacent billing features such as payment methods, tax settings, invoice templates, or plan changes out of scope unless requested.
Does not invent specific UI component names, schema fields, API endpoints, billing-provider behavior, or storage details.
Stops after the spec artifact and concise summary.

evals.name: Non-technical checkout wording
evals.prompt: I am not technical. On the checkout screen, shipping, coupons, and the final total are hard to understand. I want customers to feel confident before buying.
evals.expected_output: The agent writes a plain-language requirements spec that translates checkout concerns into observable requirements and decisions without implementation jargon.
expectations: Uses practical language suitable for a non-technical user.
Translates `feel confident before buying` into observable outcomes such as clear shipping, coupon, and final total display while keeping it as an interpretation if not confirmed.
Separates confirmed pain points from assumptions about layout, copy, calculation, and error states.
Asks no more than three direct questions in the summary; lower-impact uncertainties are proposed as defaults, assumptions, out-of-scope items, or open risks instead of extra questions.
Asks only decisions that affect user experience or business rules, such as coupon failure messaging or when shipping is known.
Defines acceptance criteria in shopping-flow terms rather than framework or database terms.
Keeps approval state unapproved if business rules remain unresolved.

evals.name: Contradictory migration scope
evals.prompt: We need to migrate saved reports to the new format, but don't change old reports and don't add compatibility code. It has to be safe and invisible to users.
evals.expected_output: The agent creates or updates a requirements spec that surfaces the contradiction between migration, unchanged old reports, no compatibility code, and invisible behavior, then stops for user decisions.
expectations: Identifies the contradiction instead of smoothing it into a confident requirement.
Separates possible interpretations such as copy-on-read, one-time migration, dual reader, or no migration.
Explains the consequence of each choice in user or data-safety terms.
Marks data compatibility and rollback or recovery expectations as blocking decisions or blocking unknowns.
Does not propose implementation details as if the contradiction were resolved.
Keeps approval state Draft until the migration contract is chosen.

evals.name: Creative dashboard brainstorming stays optional
evals.prompt: The direction is not decided yet. I want a team activity dashboard that people actually want to check every morning. Use a few creative ideas while clarifying the requirements.
evals.expected_output: The agent drafts a requirements spec with a small set of creative dashboard directions, keeps them as options until the user chooses, and asks which direction should become the requirement basis.
expectations: Uses the user's active language for the user-facing summary.
Offers two to five creative options or directions rather than one asserted solution.
Makes the creative options meaningfully distinct, not near-duplicate variants of the same dashboard idea.
For each option, includes when it fits and a practical tradeoff.
States what requirement would be adopted if the user chooses an option.
Does not treat all brainstormed ideas as confirmed requirements.
Does not write an implementation plan.
Asks which option, combination, or direction the user wants to adopt before approval.
Keeps approval state unapproved until the user chooses a direction and approves the spec.

evals.name: Ambiguous readiness keeps drafting active
evals.prompt: Using vibe-requirements-spec, finalize the spec for saved-report renaming. Signed-in users can rename a saved report inline, names must be 1-80 characters, empty names show validation, Save persists the new name, Cancel restores the previous name, duplicate names are allowed, and sharing/export changes are out of scope. Looks ready, go ahead.
evals.expected_output: The agent creates or updates only the requirements spec, treats `Looks ready, go ahead` as ambiguous handoff wording rather than explicit spec approval, leaves approval state unapproved, and asks for explicit approval of the spec.
expectations: Produces or updates a requirements spec for saved-report renaming.
Separates confirmed requirements from out-of-scope sharing and export changes.
Does not mark approval state Approved unless the wording clearly approves the current spec artifact.
Names the exact approval wording needed next, such as approving the current spec for later planning.
Explicitly treats `go ahead` wording as later-phase context rather than current-turn planning or implementation authorization.
Does not write an implementation plan, code patch, file list, test plan, command sequence, commit plan, or tool-managed implementation task list.
Does not require or name a specific downstream skill or workflow.

evals.name: New information updates same spec
evals.prompt: We already have a requirements spec at specs/report-rename-spec.md. Add that renaming should be blocked for archived reports, and keep the spec going until I approve it.
evals.expected_output: The agent updates specs/report-rename-spec.md rather than creating a new spec, records the archived-report rule and revision note, keeps approval state unapproved, and summarizes the remaining approval action.
expectations: Uses the existing path specs/report-rename-spec.md as the current spec path.
Does not create a new unrelated spec path.
Adds archived-report blocking as a confirmed requirement or decision based on wording.
Records the update in Revision notes.
Keeps approval state Draft or Awaiting explicit approval rather than Approved.
Returns a concise summary with spec path, approval state, and exact next user action.

evals.name: Explicit approval stops before planning
evals.prompt: The current spec is specs/report-rename-spec.md. I approve this spec. Use it for planning next.
evals.expected_output: The agent marks specs/report-rename-spec.md Approved and stops after the spec summary, saying the approved file can be used by a later implementation-planning phase without producing an implementation plan in the same response.
expectations: Updates the existing spec path rather than creating a new spec.
Sets approval state to Approved because the user explicitly approved the current spec.
Records what was approved in the approval note or revision notes.
Does not produce an implementation plan, implementation task list, test plan, verification command list, code patch, commit, or release work.
Refers generically to a later implementation-planning phase instead of requiring a named downstream workflow.
Stops after the spec artifact and concise summary.

evals.name: Approved spec change reopens drafting
evals.prompt: The approved spec at specs/report-rename-spec.md needs one change: archived reports should allow renaming after all. Then continue.
evals.expected_output: The agent updates the same approved spec, sets approval state to Reopened after approval, records the changed archived-report rule, and requires renewed explicit approval before later planning.
expectations: Uses specs/report-rename-spec.md as the current spec path.
Does not keep approval state Approved after the requirement change.
Sets approval state to Reopened after approval or equivalent unapproved reopened state.
Records the changed requirement and revision note.
Asks for renewed explicit approval tied to the current spec.
Does not continue into implementation planning or coding.

scoring.notes: These evals focus on observable requirements-spec artifact behavior rather than subjective writing quality. They pressure the skill's main contracts: spec file creation or update, same-spec continuity, explicit approval persistence, question-load control, broad checklist mode, downstream-workflow neutrality, scope separation, write-safety, auditability, and stop behavior after approval or handoff wording.
